title: SinkCast: An Empirical Study of Inference-Time Correction for BF16 RoPE Shift-Invariance

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to "restore BF16 RoPE shift-invariance at low overhead by correcting only attention-sink positions." This is a specific objective related to numerical precision in attention mechanisms, particularly addressing the shift-invariance issue in BF16 RoPE. None of the prior papers explicitly address this purpose. While [19] discusses attention sinks in streaming LLMs and [14], [7], and [8] explore RoPE mechanisms and extensions, none of them aim to restore BF16 RoPE shift-invariance or address this specific problem. These papers either focus on understanding or extending RoPE, or on general attention sink phenomena, but not on correcting BF16 RoPE shift-invariance.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, "SinkCast," involves running BF16 FlashAttention to obtain output and log-sum-exp statistics, selectively recomputing sink-key logits in FP32, and applying a closed-form correction to the output. This mechanism combines selective recomputation and numerical correction techniques. Papers [16] and [17] describe selective recomputation for error correction in binary neural networks, which is conceptually similar to the selective recomputation aspect of SinkCast. Additionally, [2], [4], and [20] discuss accurate computation of log-sum-exp and softmax functions, which overlaps with the numerical correction aspect of SinkCast. However, none of these papers combine selective recomputation with closed-form correction in the specific context of BF16 RoPE or attention mechanisms, making the mechanism partially related but not fully covered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses a three-stage method on Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B-v0.3 with FlashAttention-2, measuring gap closure percentages. This evaluation design is not novel. Papers [6] and [3] evaluate FlashAttention variants on LLMs, and [19] evaluates attention sinks in streaming LLMs. These prior works use similar evaluation designs involving LLMs, attention mechanisms, and performance metrics. The specific models and benchmarks differ, but the evaluation design (testing on LLMs with attention mechanisms and measuring performance improvements) is covered.

### Domain
The domain is "LLM inference / attention numerical precision (BF16 RoPE, position-independent KV caching)." Papers [7], [8], [14], and [19] all work in the general area of LLM inference and attention mechanisms, including RoPE and attention sinks. While the specific focus on BF16 RoPE and position-independent KV caching is narrower, it falls within the broader domain of LLM inference and attention numerical precision, which is covered by these prior works.

**MECHANISM: SinkCast — run BF16 FlashAttention, selectively recompute sink-key logits in FP32, apply closed-form correction using log-sum-exp statistics.**

The mechanism combines: (1) selective recomputation of specific positions in higher precision, (2) using log-sum-exp statistics from FlashAttention to apply a closed-form output correction.
